messages.content: what does she had been walking before she came inside mean?
she spent time walking before she came inside. had been walking looks back at that time from when she came in.
can you explain that in another way?
she spent time walking, then came inside. the sentence looks back at the walking from that later moment.
write a short story with a warm drink after that.

a woman had been walking through town before she came to the house of her aunt. her aunt asked whether she wanted a warm drink. she sat near the window and talked about what she saw on the way. after a while, she put her cup down and helped with the meal.
make the story shorter.
a woman had been walking through town before she came to the house of her aunt. her aunt gave her a warm drink, and they talked near the window.
does had been walking mean she is still walking inside?
not in this example. the story moves from walking through town to sitting inside. the walking happened before that.
say just what happened first and what happened next.
no. the walking happened before she sat inside. she is not walking in the room in this story.
can you write the same order without had been?
she walked through town, then came inside and sat with a warm drink.
if i say i should have asked which book, does that mean i asked?
no. you are saying that asking would have been better. the sentence does not say that you asked.
what is the person thinking about now?
you are looking back and thinking that asking was the better choice. you have not said that you really asked.
make a simple story where someone brought the wrong book.

a boy is asked to bring the blue book. there are two blue books, but he chooses without asking. when he brings it, his sister says she wanted the other one. he says he should have asked which book she wanted. then he asks for a detail to find the right one.
give just the sentence about what he should have done.
he says he should have asked which book she wanted.
what can he do now instead of only feeling wrong about it?
he can ask what the book is about or where it was on the desk. then he can use that detail to choose the right book.
make that a short answer.
ask for one more detail, then look for the book using her answer.
use choose instead of look for.
ask for one more detail, then use her answer to choose the book.
my friend says i would have helped if i had known. does that say they helped?
no. it is about help they would have given if they had known before. it is not the same as saying that they helped.
what could knowing before have changed?
no. they are saying that knowing before could have changed what they did. they have not said that the help happened.
write a kind reply if i know i did not ask them.
thank you. i did not tell you i needed help, so you did not know. i can ask another time rather than think you know without being told.
make the reply shorter.
thank you. i did not tell you i needed help. next time, i can ask.
does that mean they must always help when asked?
no. asking gives them a question to answer. they might not have time, or the task might be something they cannot do.
make that answer shorter.
no. you can ask, and they can say whether they have time and can do that task.
write a request for help tomorrow without choosing their answer.
would you have time to help me for a little while tomorrow?
what can i mean by i will have finished the letter before you come?
you are saying that the letter will be finished before the other person comes. the sentence looks at a later meeting and puts the finish before it.
explain that as a plan.
you plan to finish the letter first. the other person comes after that in your sentence.
write it without will have, using two short sentences.
i will finish the letter first. then you will come.
is that the same as asking the person to wait until i finish?
not always. you can say when you plan to finish without asking the other person to wait. if you want them to wait, you should ask.
why should i use a question if i want them to wait?
no. saying when you plan to finish is different from asking another person to wait. use a question if you want them to choose a later time.
write that question.
could you come after i finish the letter?
what if i know i will be ready by three?
then you can ask about three: would coming at three work for you? i plan to have the letter ready before then.
does a plan mean something must happen?
no. what you plan can still change if you get new information or have a problem.
say that in one short sentence.
no. a plan is what you want to do, but something new can still change it.
write a story about a hotel worker finding a note for someone in a room. keep it clear that reading the note does not make the worker the person it is for.

a hotel worker finds a note near the door of a room. it asks the person in that room to call a cousin. the worker finds out which room it is for, then gives it to the right person. that person reads it and makes the call. the worker does not call the cousin himself because the request was for the person in the room, not everyone who sees the words.
make the story shorter.
a worker finds a note for a person who is at a hotel. he finds out which room it is for and gives it to that person. the person reads it and calls the cousin who sent it.
give only the part about what the worker does.
a worker finds a note for a person who is at the hotel. he finds out which room it is for and gives it to that person.
why is who the message is for important?
because the same words can be a request for one person and only information for another. knowing the words is not enough without knowing their place in the conversation.
can the worker still help?
yes. giving the note to the right person is help. he does not need to do the task in it himself.
what question could he ask if the room is not clear?
do you know which person this note is for?
i see someone inside a bank after the door is closed. does that mean i can walk in for help?
not from that alone. someone can be working inside while the place is closed to people coming in. you need to check whether it is open for what you want to do.
write a short conversation where i ask rather than choose.
is the bank still open for people to come in? not now, i am sorry. when can i come back? please look at the time on the note by the door.
does the conversation give a real opening hour?
no. the conversation says where to look, but does not give the time written on the note. we should not add an hour we were not given.
answer with one short sentence.
no. the note may give a time, but the conversation did not give that detail.
can a made up conversation still help me write a question for a real place?
yes. you can use the question, then get the real answer from the people or information at that place. the example should not become a fact about every bank.
write just the question about coming back.
when would be a good time for me to come back for help?
what should i do with an answer i am not sure i understood?
ask them to say it again or write the time clearly. it is better to check when a detail is not clear.
why could asking again help?
if you understand the time, you can choose when to go back. without that detail, you might go back while the bank is still closed.
give just the request.
ask them to say it again so you know when to come back.
my cousin lives in another country. if it is cold at my house, can i say it is cold at theirs too?
not just because you are in the same family. places can have different weather. you would need information about where your cousin is, rather than use your own weather as their answer.
write a short message asking about it.
what is the weather like where you are today? it is cold here.
what if they send a picture with snow but do not say when it was taken?
you can ask when they took it. an old picture may not tell you what the weather is like today.
write a kind question about when they took it.
when did you take this picture? is that what it looks like there today?
make the question shorter.
when was this picture taken?
they say it is from last year. what do i know now?
you know the picture is from last year. you still do not know the weather there today unless they give a new detail.
can i say there is no snow there now?
not from that information alone. an old picture does not tell us every change after it was taken.
write a question to get the information i need.
is there snow where you are today?
picoboi, write she brought it after i say my aunt and my sister were both near the book. do you know who she is?
not from that alone. both your aunt and sister could be she. i should ask which person you mean before making the sentence specific.
ask that question.
do you mean your aunt or your sister brought the book?
my aunt. now make it a clear sentence with aunt instead of she.
my aunt brought the book.
why did you not just choose my sister because i wrote sister last?
being last is not enough to make your sister the right person. both people could have brought the book, so asking helps make your meaning clear.
why was my answer important?
you gave two possible people. i needed your answer to know which one the sentence was about.
say which people were possible.
your aunt and sister were both possible. your answer made the right person clear.
now my sister brought the cup too. put both facts together.
my aunt brought the book, and my sister brought the cup.
does too say she brought the book as well?
not in that sentence. it can add another fact about the cup. if the meaning is not clear, name what each person brought.
